question.prompt: The sum of all but one of the interior angles of a convex polygon equals \(2570^\circ.\) The remaining angle is

solutions.explanation:
Let \(\theta\) be the remaining interior angle. Convexity gives \(0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ\), so the full interior angle sum satisfies
\[2570^\circ<2570^\circ+\theta<2750^\circ.\]
For an \(n\)-sided polygon, where \(n\ge3\) is an integer, the full sum is \((n-2)180^\circ\). It must therefore be a multiple of \(180^\circ\).

The neighboring multiples are \(2520^\circ\), \(2700^\circ\), and \(2880^\circ\), so only \(2700^\circ\) lies in the required interval. Consequently,
\[\theta=2700^\circ-2570^\circ=130^\circ.\]
The answer is choice D.
